nodes.name: Platform Operator
nodes.description: Registers hosts and zones as Host and AvailabilityZone objects, creates each host's SSH Secret in the credentials namespace, and cordons hosts. Never runs commands on a hypervisor by hand once faubourg manages it.

nodes.name: VM Consumer
nodes.description: Requests VMs, pools or claims from banlieue and targets a zone with a providerSelector on the faubourg zone label (ADR-0003). Never sees faubourg objects.

nodes.name: faubourg
nodes.description: The control plane: inventory of hosts, grouping into availability zones, remote bootstrap, zone health. Ships no host agent and no VM scheduler (ADR-0002).

nodes.name: Host controller
nodes.description: The faubourg-controller Deployment in faubourg-system: two replicas, of which only the leader elected through a Lease acts, and it stops before its lease can lapse (ADR-0009, ADR-0014). Reconciles Host: gates on the zone, applies the host's banlieue Provider (class, endpoint and labels for a bootstrapped host, labels only for an adopted one; never deletes one, ADR-0011), creates the bootstrap Job once banlieue has given the Provider its identity and when the Host's bootstrap inputs change (the pinned script digest among them), holding a re-bootstrap of an already-bootstrapped host until a rollout slot is free and halting the rollout at the first failure (ADR-0013), derives the phase from the Job and the Provider (ADR-0005, ADR-0007), writes status by server-side apply, and drains a Host whose spec.maintenance is Drain: it cordons the Provider, then asks banlieue to move the Host's VMs one at a time by creating VirtualMachineMoves with no target, reports Drained (MovesBlocked naming the VMs banlieue would not move), and on maintenance None deletes its moves that have not reached HandingOver (ADR-0017). It never updates or deletes a VirtualMachine. Never reads SSH Secrets, a script or any ConfigMap but the bootstrap policy parameters, never mints a token. The Provider's class is the zone's (or --provider-class), and its endpoint and required deployment mode come from a driver chosen by the class's backend, from a closed set (cloud-hypervisor today; anything else ProviderBackendUnsupported, for bootstrapped and adopted Hosts alike); a Host whose existing Provider has another class is ProviderClassMismatch, and two Hosts with one literal, case-folded address are both DuplicateAddress (ADR-0018). Drivers: cloud-hypervisor and libvirt; a libvirt zone without spec.libvirt, or a cloud-hypervisor zone with one, is ProviderConnectionInvalid. A Managed (libvirt) Host is healthy on Ready and ProviderReachable for the current generation, not on the Lease (ProviderUnreachable otherwise); its Job is created without waiting for an identity; a drain on a backend banlieue cannot move cordons and reports MovesUnsupported. A Provider write the API server refuses (RBAC, faubourg-provider-connection, or banlieue's credentialsRef policy, which since banlieue ADR-0157 accepts the controller's reference grant on Secrets in banlieue's namespace in place of get) fails the Host with ProviderApplyRefused. Planned (roadmap 04): the firecracker driver, once banlieue ships the class.

nodes.name: Zone controller
nodes.description: Runs in faubourg-controller beside the Host controller, only on the replica holding the leader Lease (ADR-0014). Writes each AvailabilityZone's status by server-side apply under faubourg.firestoned.io/zone-controller, and nothing else: hosts, readyHosts, cordonedHosts and Ready (StorageModeUnsupported, InvalidSpec, NoHosts, NoReadyHost, AllReadyHostsCordoned, HostsReady), a pure function of the zone and its Hosts. Also HostsMatch (HostsDiffer, HostsUnreported), advisory: whether every member's Provider reports the same raw.vmm and raw.cpuModel, which banlieue requires to move a VM between them (ADR-0017 decision 9). A report, not a gate: nothing faubourg decides reads it (ADR-0004, ADR-0015). Reads the zone's ProviderClass and reports ProviderBackendUnsupported for a class it does not drive (ADR-0018 decision 2). Reports ProviderConnectionInvalid when the zone's libvirt connection does not fit its backend. A backend whose Providers do not publish raw.vmm and raw.cpuModel (libvirt) reports HostsUnreported.

nodes.name: Bootstrap Job
nodes.description: One Kubernetes Job per set of a Host's bootstrap inputs (ADR-0009 decision 6), in the credentials namespace (ADR-0005 decision 5). Runs faubourg-bootstrap (ADR-0010): one static Rust binary on russh in an image with no shell, digest-pinned. It refuses a mounted script whose sha256 is not the pinned FAUBOURG_SCRIPT_SHA256 before opening any connection (exit 66, ScriptUnpinned, ADR-0013), and a mounted provider CA whose sha256 is not the pinned FAUBOURG_PROVIDER_CA_SHA256 (exit 67, ProviderCAUnpinned), which it then writes into the host's kubeconfig instead of the cluster CA (ADR-0016), verifies the host key before authenticating (Strict whenever the Secret has knownHosts), checks the on-host script's owner, mode and sha256 with the scoped credential, places it and the sudo rule with the privileged placement credential only when it differs (else ScriptDrift), optionally revokes the placement key, then runs sudo -n /opt/faubourg/install.sh. Every command is a constant; data goes on stdin. Mints the host's first provider token through TokenRequest with its own 10-minute projected token, and hands it to the install script on stdin, never to the controller or a Secret (ADR-0011). Reports the host key fingerprint in its termination message (ADR-0005, ADR-0006, ADR-0008, ADR-0010). For a Managed (libvirt) backend the Job has no provider variables, no kube-api volume and no provider CA: it mints no token and sends the script nothing (ADR-0018 decision 7).

nodes.name: Bootstrap admission policy
nodes.description: A ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and binding on the credentials namespace, evaluated by the Kubernetes API server. Every Job there must run the digest-pinned bootstrap image with no command, literal env, read-only credential volumes and a script volume whose source, key and FAUBOURG_SCRIPT_SHA256 match a pinned entry and the restricted security profile; only the Job controller may create Pods there. Parameters live in a ConfigMap in faubourg-system that neither the controller nor a script maintainer can write (ADR-0008, ADR-0013). The token policy admits a TokenRequest only for a name under one of providerServiceAccountPrefixes, one banlieue-provider-<class>- entry per External class in use; a bare prefix or an empty entry admits nothing (ADR-0018 decision 5).

nodes.name: Bootstrap policy parameters (A-8)
nodes.description: The ConfigMap faubourg-bootstrap-policy in faubourg-system, written by the platform administrator: the bootstrap image's digest, and each allowed script source with its key and the sha256 of its content (ConfigMap/<name>/<key>@sha256:<hex>). The admission policy evaluates every Job against it; the Host controller reads it, and nothing else of its kind, to learn each script's pinned digest. Optionally pins the CA the hosts trust for the API server, providerCASource, the same way (ADR-0016). A script maintainer cannot pin their own change (ADR-0008, ADR-0013, ADR-0016).

nodes.name: Controller leader Lease
nodes.description: The coordination.k8s.io/v1 Lease faubourg-controller in faubourg-system. Its holder is the one controller replica that acts. Acquired and taken over by conditional writes, so one candidate wins; renewed every 5 seconds; the leader exits if it has not renewed within 10, before the 15-second lease can lapse (ADR-0014).

nodes.name: Host and AvailabilityZone CRs
nodes.description: Cluster-scoped faubourg.firestoned.io/v1alpha1 objects; the Rust types in faubourg-api are the source of truth (ADR-0003).

nodes.name: Host SSH Secret
nodes.description: Root-equivalent bootstrap credential, one per host, in the credentials namespace. Key or SSH certificate preferred, password discouraged, knownHosts pins the host key (ADR-0006).

nodes.name: Kubernetes API server
nodes.description: The only transport between faubourg and banlieue: CRDs, Jobs, Leases.

nodes.name: banlieue
nodes.description: VM lifecycle platform. Its controller, scheduler and operator place VMs across Provider failure domains, read provider Leases, and run nothing on the hosts directly; a Managed provider (libvirt) runs in the cluster and dials its host (banlieue ADR-0060, ADR-0098, ADR-0102).

nodes.name: banlieue Provider (one per host)
nodes.description: Class: the zone's ProviderClass (ADR-0018). Endpoint ch://<address> for cloud-hypervisor; for libvirt qemu+tls://<address>/system with the zone's credentialsRef and caBundle (configMapRef), never insecureSkipTLSVerify. Planned (roadmap 04): firecracker's scheme. Created by faubourg with the zone, host and cordon labels it owns by field manager, and banlieue's zone key banlieue.io/zone while the Host's zone exists and is valid (ADR-0017 decision 1: the statement that lets banlieue move a VM between the zone's hosts, banlieue ADR-0127); its status (failure domain, capacity, Ready) is written by banlieue's provider for that host (ADR-0003, ADR-0007). Created and labelled by faubourg for a bootstrapped host, labelled only for an adopted one (ADR-0011).

nodes.name: banlieue VirtualMachines and VirtualMachineMoves
nodes.description: banlieue's namespaced VirtualMachine (status.scheduled names the Provider a VM runs on) and VirtualMachineMove (a request that banlieue move one running VM to another host of its zone; banlieue ADR-0127, API from banlieue v0.5.7). faubourg reads VMs cluster-wide and creates, lists and deletes the moves it labelled with a Host's name; banlieue admits, ranks the destination and performs each move.

nodes.name: Cloud Hypervisor or Firecracker host
nodes.description: A bare-metal KVM machine whose zone's ProviderClass has an External backend (ADR-0018 decision 2): cloud-hypervisor, prepared by banlieue host cloud-hypervisor install, or, planned (roadmap 04), firecracker, once banlieue ships that class (its roadmap 20). One VMM per host: a host is one class, never both.

nodes.name: Install script source
nodes.description: ConfigMap or Secret holding install.sh, in the credentials namespace and on the admission policy's scriptSources allowlist with the sha256 of its content; an edit runs nowhere until the platform administrator pins it. The default downloads a pinned banlieue binary, verifies its sha256 and runs banlieue host cloud-hypervisor install (ADR-0005, ADR-0008, ADR-0013).

nodes.name: /opt/faubourg/install.sh
nodes.description: root:root 0755 under a root-owned directory; the scoped account's only sudo rule runs it with no arguments, and cannot write it (ADR-0005).

nodes.name: sshd
nodes.description: The host's SSH daemon. Reached only by bootstrap Jobs, and optionally closed to faubourg after bootstrap (ssh.revokeAfterBootstrap).

nodes.name: banlieue host-resident provider
nodes.description: Host-resident systemd service, outbound only to the Kubernetes API, supervising one VMM process per guest through template units (banlieue ADR-0060, ADR-0063). For cloud-hypervisor today; for firecracker, planned (roadmap 04). This is the host agent of an External backend (ADR-0002, amended by ADR-0018).

nodes.name: VMM (one per VM)
nodes.description: cloud-hypervisor, or firecracker (planned, roadmap 04), with its API on a local unix socket, started by the provider as a systemd template unit instance.

nodes.name: Host management network
nodes.description: The path from cluster nodes to each host's SSH port and from each host to the Kubernetes API. Exact topology is an open question (ADR-0005).

nodes.name: GitHub Container Registry
nodes.description: Holds faubourg-controller and faubourg-bootstrap, pushed only from main and releases, each Cosign-signed keyless by digest with build provenance and an SBOM (ADR-0012).

nodes.name: Install file (faubourg-<version>.yaml)
nodes.description: deploy/ rendered with both image digests by make release-manifests, Cosign-signed, attached to each release. The bootstrap digest is written into the admission policy's parameters and the controller's environment by the same render (ADR-0012).

nodes.name: banlieue ProviderClass
nodes.description: Cluster-scoped banlieue object. A zone names one (spec.providerClassRef, immutable; omitted, the controller's --provider-class). faubourg reads its spec.backend and spec.deployment and picks a driver from a closed set: cloud-hypervisor and firecracker External, libvirt Managed; anything else is ProviderBackendUnsupported and its Hosts get no Provider and no Job (ADR-0011, ADR-0018 decision 2). Written by banlieue's administrator, never by faubourg.

nodes.name: libvirt host
nodes.description: A bare-metal KVM machine in a zone whose class has backend libvirt (ADR-0018). Runs sshd and /opt/faubourg/install.sh (examples/host/install-libvirt.sh) exactly as a host-resident host does (shown once, on that host); the install script sets up libvirtd with TLS and reads nothing on stdin (ADR-0018 decision 7). No banlieue process runs on it.

nodes.name: libvirtd
nodes.description: libvirt's daemon, listening for TLS on 16514 with auth_tls none: the client certificate is the credential (banlieue ADR-0011). Its server certificate comes from the install script or is already on the host. QEMU guests.

nodes.name: banlieue libvirt provider
nodes.description: A Managed banlieue provider: a Deployment per Provider in banlieue's namespace, run by banlieue's operator, which grants it get on exactly the Secret and ConfigMap its Provider names. Dials qemu+tls://<address>/system and publishes one failure domain named after the Provider, carrying its labels. Its Lease is renewed in the cluster, so it is not the host's heartbeat (ADR-0018 decision 8).

nodes.name: libvirt client credential and CA
nodes.description: Per zone (ADR-0018 decision 6): a Secret (tls.crt, tls.key) and a ConfigMap (libvirtd's server CA) in banlieue's namespace, created by the operator and named with the faubourg- prefix. The zone references them; faubourg copies the names into each member's Provider and never reads either. Whoever holds the key can drive libvirtd on every host of the zone.

nodes.name: Provider connection admission policy
nodes.description: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy faubourg-provider-connection, evaluated by the Kubernetes API server on Provider writes by faubourg's controller ServiceAccount: a credentialsRef must start with faubourg-, so a compromised controller cannot point a libvirt Provider at another Provider's credential (ADR-0018 decision 6).

relationships.description: faubourg is two reconcilers, the Jobs one of them creates and the admission policy that constrains those Jobs, guarding the inventory objects.
What runs on a prepared host.
banlieue's objects faubourg writes and reads, and its in-cluster provider for Managed backends.
Hosts sit on the management network.
The operator declares hosts, zones and SSH Secrets.
The consumer asks banlieue for VMs and may select a zone by label.

Watches Host (every Host, for DuplicateAddress), AvailabilityZone, ProviderClass, its own Jobs (by owner UID) in the credentials namespace and Providers in banlieue's namespace; reads Pods there for a failed Job's exit code and a succeeded Job's host key fingerprint (ADR-0010 decision 8); creates and deletes Jobs; applies Host status. No Secret or ConfigMap access in the credentials namespace; every Job it creates passes the bootstrap admission policy (ADR-0008, ADR-0009). In banlieue's namespace it holds reference, and never get, list or watch, on Secrets, so banlieue's credentialsRef policy admits a libvirt Provider naming the zone's credential (ADR-0018 amended, banlieue ADR-0157); faubourg-provider-connection bounds which it may name.
The API server evaluates the policy on every Job and Pod create or update in the credentials namespace, before the object exists. Deny on failure.
The admission policy evaluates every Job with the parameters: the pinned image, and the pinned script source, key and digest (ADR-0008, ADR-0013).
The Host controller gets, lists and watches this one ConfigMap by name, read-only, to resolve each Host's script to its pinned digest (ADR-0013).
Each replica gets, creates and updates this one Lease: the leader renews it, a standby waits to take it over, a leader shutting down releases it (ADR-0014).
Reads AvailabilityZones, Hosts, the members' Providers and the zone's ProviderClass; patches availabilityzones/status only (ADR-0015, ADR-0017).
The Job's pod mounts exactly one host's Secret(s) as a read-only volume; the controller never fetches them, and the admission policy keeps any other image from mounting them (ADR-0008).
The Job mounts the script source, refuses it unless its sha256 is the pinned digest, and compares it with the on-host script.

SSH (CALM has no SSH protocol value). Strict host key verification (or recorded TOFU). Placement with the privileged credential when needed, then the one scoped sudo command; no CR field reaches a shell (ADR-0005). Host key verified before any authentication (ADR-0010 decision 4). The same for every backend (ADR-0018 decision 4).
Outbound only: renews its Lease every 5 seconds and writes its Provider status and machines (banlieue ADR-0060, ADR-0102).
The VMM REST API over the guest's unix socket (banlieue ADR-0061).
banlieue's scheduler reads each Provider's failure domain, labels, capacity and heartbeat to place VMs (banlieue ADR-0098, ADR-0107).

banlieue admits each VirtualMachineMove (same zone, matching VMM and CPU model, the move feature, the VM's own policy and placement), picks the destination with the most free memory after the move, and moves the VM through the two hosts' providers (banlieue ADR-0127; its controller ships with Stage 1).

Applies the host's Provider, named after the Host, by server-side apply: the zone, host, cordon and zone labels, and banlieue.io/zone for a member of a valid zone, under faubourg.firestoned.io/host-controller for every host, and the class and endpoint under faubourg.firestoned.io/host-provider-spec for a bootstrapped one only, so a host switched to adopted keeps its spec. Reads its health from the one Provider carrying the host label (ADR-0003, ADR-0007, ADR-0009, ADR-0011). The class is the zone's and the endpoint the backend's (ADR-0018). For libvirt the spec manager also owns connection.credentialsRef and connection.caBundle, from the zone, admitted by faubourg-provider-connection.

Draining a Host (ADR-0017): lists banlieue VirtualMachines in every namespace to find those scheduled on the Host's Provider (get, list, watch; no update or patch), and creates one VirtualMachineMove per VM in the VM's namespace, labelled with the Host's name and with no target, at most MAX_MOVES_PER_HOST in flight; deletes its moves still Pending, Preparing or Copying when maintenance is cleared (create, get, list, watch, delete). A missing VirtualMachineMove CRD fails closed: Drained=False, MovesUnsupported, nothing created.

Requests a day's token for the host Provider's ServiceAccount (TokenRequest), as faubourg-bootstrap with a 10-minute projected token; bounded by RBAC and the faubourg-provider-tokens admission policy to provider ServiceAccounts of the listed External classes (ADR-0018 decision 5). Only for External backends, at most a day, no audience or binding (ADR-0011).
The kubelet pulls the controller and bootstrap images by digest; the admission policy admits only the bootstrap digest the operator applied (ADR-0008, ADR-0012).
The operator verifies the install file's and the images' signatures, sets the API server address, and applies it (ADR-0012).
What runs on a prepared libvirt host, besides sshd and the install script.
Reads and watches the zone's ProviderClass (get, list, watch; cluster-scoped) for its backend and deployment mode, and picks the driver; no write (ADR-0011, ADR-0018).
Reads (get, list, watch) the zone's ProviderClass to report ProviderBackendUnsupported (ADR-0018 decision 2).
The API server evaluates faubourg-provider-connection on every Provider create or update by faubourg's controller that changes its connection, before the object is written. Deny on failure.
Gets the Secret and ConfigMap its Provider names, by name, under the Role banlieue's operator gives it (banlieue ADR-0003).

Libvirt's RPC over mutual TLS to port 16514, the client certificate as the credential, the server verified against the zone's CA (banlieue ADR-0011). From the cluster to the host: a path host-resident hosts do not need.
Renews its Lease and writes its Provider's status, failure domain and Ready and ProviderReachable conditions.

flows.name: Add a host-resident (Cloud Hypervisor or Firecracker) host to a zone
flows.description: From a new Host object to a host banlieue can place VMs on.

transitions.description: Operator creates the SSH Secret and a Host with zoneRef.

Host controller checks the zone and its ProviderClass's backend (External for a host-resident provider), applies the host's Provider, waits for banlieue to give it an identity, then creates the bootstrap Job; phase Bootstrapping.
The Job's pod mounts that host's Secret(s) and the script source.
The Job mints the provider's first token, verifies the host key, places the script if absent or changed, and runs sudo -n /opt/faubourg/install.sh with the credential on stdin.
The install script installs the credential where banlieue's provider reads it; the Provider carries faubourg's zone labels (ADR-0011).
The host-resident provider starts, renews its Lease and publishes its failure domain.
Provider Ready and heartbeat Alive: Host Ready; banlieue may place VMs on it.

flows.name: Add a libvirt host to a zone
flows.description: From a new Host in a libvirt zone to a host banlieue can place VMs on (ADR-0018).

transitions.description: Operator creates the zone's faubourg- prefixed client credential and CA in banlieue's namespace, a zone naming a libvirt ProviderClass, the SSH Secret and the Host.
Host controller reads the class: backend libvirt, Managed; picks the libvirt driver.
It applies the Provider with qemu+tls://<address>/system and the zone's credentialsRef and caBundle; faubourg-provider-connection admits the faubourg- name.
The Job, with no kube-api volume, verifies the host key, places the script if needed and runs sudo -n /opt/faubourg/install.sh, which sets up libvirtd with TLS.
banlieue's in-cluster libvirt provider dials the host with the zone's client certificate and publishes one failure domain.
Provider Ready and ProviderReachable for its generation: Host Ready; banlieue may place VMs on it.

metadata.project: faubourg: availability zones over banlieue's bare-metal hosts
metadata.phase: Roadmaps 00 to 02 done, 03 and 04 in progress: Cloud Hypervisor and libvirt zones, bootstrap, zone health, cordon and drain. Firecracker (roadmap 04 phase D) is marked planned.
